content: Lansoprazole is a medication primarily used to treat conditions caused by excessive stomach acid. These include heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), stomach ulcers, and erosive esophagitis. It is also used to manage conditions where the stomach produces too much acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, and to treat infections caused by Helicobacter pylori when combined with antibiotics. Lansoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. It is available in various forms, including delayed-release oral capsules (15 mg and 30 mg) and orally disintegrating tablets (15 mg and 30 mg). It should be taken before meals, and the capsules or tablets should not be chewed, crushed, or split. If swallowing is difficult, the capsule contents can be sprinkled on certain soft foods like applesauce and consumed immediately. Common side effects of lansoprazole include diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, and constipation. If these symptoms persist or worsen, consult your healthcare provider. Serious side effects, though less common, include kidney problems (acute interstitial nephritis), severe diarrhea caused by Clostridioides difficile infection, and severe skin reactions such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN). If you experience symptoms like decreased urine output, blood in the urine, persistent diarrhea, skin rash, or peeling skin, seek medical attention immediately. Lansoprazole may also cause vitamin B12 deficiency, especially with long-term use (over three years), and low magnesium levels (hypomagnesemia), which can lead to muscle spasms, seizures, or heart rhythm problems. Long-term use may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures, particularly in older adults or those taking high doses. This medication can interact with other drugs, including methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, theophylline, certain antibiotics (e.g., clarithromycin), and antiretroviral medications (e.g., rilpivirine). It may also interact with supplements like St. John’s Wort. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications, supplements, and herbal products you are taking to avoid potential interactions. Lansoprazole is not recommended for immediate relief of heartburn, as it may take 1 to 4 days to achieve full effectiveness. It should not be used in children under 2 years of age due to potential risks, including heart valve thickening observed in animal studies. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult their healthcare provider before using lansoprazole, as its effects on pregnancy and breast milk are not fully understood. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is close to the time for your next dose. Do not double doses. In case of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention or contact a poison control center. Store lansoprazole at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C) and protect it from extreme temperatures. Keep it out of reach of children and do not share it with others, even if they have similar symptoms. Always follow your healthcare provider’s instructions for use.
